17.         frame,
18.         kframe::KernelFrame,
19.         upool::{
20.             Upool,
21.             UserFrame,
22.         },
23.     },
24. };
25. use ::alloc::vec::Vec;
26. use ::arch::mem;
27. use ::core::{
28.     hint::unlikely,
29.     mem::MaybeUninit,
30.     sync::atomic::{
31.         AtomicBool,
32.         Ordering,
33.     },
34. };
35. use ::sys::error::{
36.     Error,
37.     ErrorCode,
38. };
39. 
40. //==================================================================================================
41. // Constants
42. //==================================================================================================
43. 
44. // Use relaxed ordering for all atomic operations to mitigate synchronization overhead. It is safe
45. // to use this ordering semantics because Nanvix is a single-core system, and the kernel runs with
46. // interrupts disabled.
47. const ORDER: Ordering = Ordering::Relaxed;
48. 
49. //==================================================================================================
50. // Global Variables
51. //==================================================================================================
52. 
53. /// Physical memory manager storage.
54. static mut PHYS_MEMORY_MANAGER: MaybeUninit<PhysMemoryManager> = MaybeUninit::uninit();
55. 
56. /// Whether the physical memory manager has been initialized.
57. static PHYS_MEMORY_MANAGER_INIT: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);
58. 
59. //==================================================================================================
60. // Structures
61. //==================================================================================================
62. 
63. ///
64. /// # Description
65. ///
66. /// Physical memory manager.
67. ///
68. #[verus_verify]
69. pub struct PhysMemoryManager {
70.     upool: Upool,
71. }
72. 
73. //==================================================================================================
74. // Implementations
75. //==================================================================================================
76. 
77. impl PhysMemoryManager {
78.     ///
79.     /// # Description
80.     ///
81.     /// Initializes the physical memory manager singleton.
82.     ///
83.     /// # Parameters
84.     ///
85.     /// - `upool`: User page pool.
86.     ///
87.     /// # Errors
88.     ///
89.     /// Returns `InvalidArgument` if the singleton has already been initialized.
90.     ///
91.     // Trusted shim: writes the `static mut` singleton storage and an `AtomicBool`
92.     // lifecycle gate (raw global state Verus cannot model). The manager-singleton
93.     // lifecycle flag is distinct from the frame-allocator lifecycle and has no
94.     // abstract model (the do-not-modify `PhysMemView` only tracks the allocator);
95.     // the contract therefore states the caller-relevant guarantee: the global
96.     // frame allocator stays initialized and well-formed across this call.
97.     #[cfg_attr(verus_keep_ghost, allow(verus_impl_method_marker))]
98.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
99.     #[verus_spec(result =>
100.         requires
101.             phys_view().initialized,
102.             phys_view().inv(),
103.         ensures
104.             phys_view().inv(),
105.             phys_view().initialized,
106.     )]
107.     pub(super) fn init(upool: Upool) -> Result<(), Error> {
108.         if unlikely(PHYS_MEMORY_MANAGER_INIT.load(ORDER)) {
109.             return Err(Error::new(
110.                 ErrorCode::InvalidArgument,
111.                 "physical memory manager already initialized",
112.             ));
113.         }
114. 
115.         // SAFETY: this happens during kernel initialization and no other threads are running.
116.         unsafe { PHYS_MEMORY_MANAGER.write(PhysMemoryManager { upool }) };
117.         PHYS_MEMORY_MANAGER_INIT.store(true, ORDER);
118.         Ok(())
119.     }
120. 
121.     ///
122.     /// # Description
123.     ///
124.     /// Gets a mutable reference to the physical memory manager.
125.     ///
126.     /// # Panics
127.     ///
128.     /// Panics if the physical memory manager is not initialized.
129.     ///
130.     /// # Safety
131.     ///
132.     /// This function is unsafe because it returns a mutable reference to a global variable.
133.     ///
134.     /// The caller must ensure:
135.     ///
136.     /// - No other `&mut PhysMemoryManager` reference obtained from this function is live at the
137.     ///   same time (i.e., `&mut` references must not overlap). In practice this is guaranteed
138.     ///   because the kernel is single-threaded and runs with interrupts disabled, so no
139.     ///   re-entrant or concurrent call can alias the reference.
140.     ///
141.     pub unsafe fn get_mut<'a>() -> &'a mut PhysMemoryManager {
142.         if unlikely(!PHYS_MEMORY_MANAGER_INIT.load(ORDER)) {
143.             panic!("physical memory manager is not initialized");
144.         }
145. 
146.         // SAFETY: the physical memory manager has been initialized, so the value is valid.
147.         PHYS_MEMORY_MANAGER.assume_init_mut()
148.     }
149. 
150.     ///
151.     /// # Description
152.     ///
153.     /// Allocates user frames into caller-provided storage.
154.     ///
155.     /// The returned frames are not guaranteed to be physically contiguous.
156.     /// User allocations are gated by the kernel watermark: if fulfilling the request would
157.     /// leave fewer than `KERNEL_WATERMARK` free frames, the allocation is rejected.
158.     ///
159.     /// # Parameters
160.     ///
161.     /// - `count`: Number of frames to allocate.
162.     /// - `frames`: Mutable reference to a pre-allocated vector into which to store those
163.     ///   frames' addresses. It should have sufficient capacity for `count` entries.
164.     ///
165.     /// # Return Values
166.     ///
167.     /// Upon success, `Ok(())` is returned and `frames` is filled with `count` frames. Upon failure, an
168.     /// error is returned and any frames allocated by this call are dropped by truncating `frames`
169.     /// back to empty.
170.     ///
171.     // Trusted shim: loops over the global frame allocator (`Upool::alloc`) and the
172.     // caller-provided `Vec`, with `error!`-logging and a clear()-on-error rollback
173.     // that Verus cannot body-verify without editing exec code. The contract is
174.     // stated over `phys_view()` and `frames@`: on success exactly `count` frames
175.     // are handed out (each now allocated); on error the vector is emptied
176.     // (all-or-nothing). Frames are not claimed contiguous.
177.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
178.     #[verus_spec(result =>
179.         requires
180.             phys_view().initialized,
181.             phys_view().inv(),
182.             old(frames)@.len() == 0,
183.         ensures
184.             phys_view().inv(),
185.             phys_view().initialized,
186.             match result {
187.                 Ok(()) => {
188.                     &&& final(frames)@.len() == count
189.                     &&& forall|i: int|
190.                         0 <= i < count as int ==>
191.                             #[trigger] phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(final(frames)@[i]@)
192.                     &&& phys_view().frames.free_frames.finite()
193.                     &&& spec_watermark_ok(phys_view().frames, 0)
194.                 },
195.                 Err(_) => final(frames)@.len() == 0,
196.             },
197.     )]
198.     pub fn alloc_many_user_frames(
199.         &mut self,
200.         count: usize,
201.         frames: &mut Vec<UserFrame>,
202.     ) -> Result<(), Error> {
203.         if !frames.is_empty() {
204.             let reason: &str = "frames vector is not empty";
205.             error!("{reason}");
206.             return Err(Error::new(ErrorCode::InvalidArgument, reason));
207.         }
208.         if frames.capacity() < count {
209.             let reason: &str = "frames vector has insufficient capacity";
210.             error!("{reason}");
211.             return Err(Error::new(ErrorCode::InvalidArgument, reason));
212.         }
213. 
214.         // A zero-sized allocation is trivially satisfied.
215.         if count == 0 {
216.             return Ok(());
217.         }
218. 
219.         Self::check_user_watermark(count)?;
220. 
221.         for _ in 0..count {
222.             match self.upool.alloc() {
223.                 Ok(frame) => frames.push(frame),
224.                 Err(error) => {
225.                     frames.clear();
226.                     return Err(error);
227.                 },
228.             }
229.         }
230.         Ok(())
231.     }

238.     /// hot paths such as copy-on-write fault resolution, where allocating an
239.     /// intermediate [`Vec`] would be wasteful.
240.     ///
241.     /// # Returns
242.     ///
243.     /// Upon success, a [`UserFrame`] is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned
244.     /// instead.
245.     ///
246.     // Trusted shim: applies the watermark gate then delegates to the global
247.     // `Upool::alloc`. On success the returned frame's physical address is now in
248.     // the allocator's `allocated_frames` and is page-aligned.

275.     /// Rejects user allocations of `count` frames that would breach the kernel
276.     /// watermark, i.e. that would drop the number of free frames below
277.     /// [`config::kernel::KERNEL_WATERMARK`].
278.     ///
279.     /// # Parameters
280.     ///
281.     /// - `count`: Number of user frames the caller intends to allocate.
282.     ///
283.     /// # Returns
284.     ///
285.     /// Upon success, `Ok(())` is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
286.     ///
287.     // Trusted shim: reads the global free-frame count and compares it against
288.     // `KERNEL_WATERMARK + count`. Pure gate, no allocator state change. `Ok` exactly

308.             .checked_add(count)
309.             .ok_or_else(|| {
310.                 let reason: &str = "watermark + count overflow";
311.                 error!("{reason}");
312.                 Error::new(ErrorCode::InvalidArgument, reason)
313.             })?;
314.         if frame::free_count() < watermark_threshold {
315.             let reason: &str = "would breach kernel watermark";
316.             error!("{reason}");
317.             return Err(Error::new(ErrorCode::OutOfMemory, reason));

326.     ///

329.     /// # Return Values
330.     ///
331.     /// Upon success, a kernel frame is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
332.     ///

334.     // watermark) and wraps it, freeing the raw frame if wrapping fails. On success
335.     // the returned frame's base address is now allocated and page-aligned.

353.         let frame_addr: FrameAddress = frame::alloc()?;
354.         KernelFrame::new(frame_addr).inspect_err(|e| {
355.             warn!("failed to wrap frame after KernelFrame::new failure: {e:?}");
356.             if let Err(free_err) = frame::free(frame_addr) {

359.         })

365.     /// Allocates a contiguous range of kernel frames into caller-provided storage.
366.     ///

368.     /// mapping and the hardware stack pointer traverses the region linearly.
369.     /// Kernel allocations bypass the watermark — no artificial ceiling.
370.     ///
371.     /// # Parameters
372.     ///
373.     /// - `count`: Number of frames to allocate.

375.     ///   those frames' addresses.

380.     /// contiguous entries. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.

383.     // (bypassing the watermark) and wraps each frame, with a two-phase
384.     // (`Vec::clear` + `frame::free`) rollback Verus cannot body-verify without
385.     // editing exec code. On success exactly `count` frames are handed out, each now
386.     // allocated, and their base addresses form an ascending page-stride run
387.     // (contiguity is load-bearing for kernel stacks). On error the vector is emptied.

390.         requires
391.             phys_view().initialized,
392.             phys_view().inv(),
393.             old(frames)@.len() == 0,
394.         ensures
395.             phys_view().inv(),
396.             phys_view().initialized,
397.             match result {
398.                 Ok(()) => {
399.                     &&& final(frames)@.len() == count
400.                     &&& forall|i: int|
401.                         0 <= i < count as int ==>
402.                             #[trigger] phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(final(frames)@[i]@)

404.                         #[trigger] kernel_frames_contiguous(final(frames)@, base)
405.                 },
406.                 Err(_) => final(frames)@.len() == 0,
407.             },
408.     )]
409.     pub fn alloc_many_kernel_frames(
410.         &mut self,
411.         count: usize,
412.         frames: &mut Vec<KernelFrame>,
413.     ) -> Result<(), Error> {
414.         // Check if caller-provided vector is not empty.
415.         if !frames.is_empty() {
416.             let reason: &str = "frames vector is not empty";
417.             error!("{reason}");
418.             return Err(Error::new(ErrorCode::InvalidArgument, reason));
419.         }
420.         if frames.capacity() < count {
421.             let reason: &str = "frames vector has insufficient capacity";
422.             error!("{reason}");
423.             return Err(Error::new(ErrorCode::InvalidArgument, reason));
424.         }
425. 
426.         let base_addr: FrameAddress = frame::alloc_contiguous(count)?;
427.         let base_raw: usize = base_addr.into_raw_value();
428.         for i in 0..count {
429.             let raw_addr: usize = base_raw + i * mem::PAGE_SIZE;
430.             match FrameAddress::from_raw_value(raw_addr).and_then(KernelFrame::new) {
431.                 Ok(kf) => frames.push(kf),
432.                 Err(e) => {
433.                     // Drop already-wrapped frames (frees them via KernelFrame::Drop).
434.                     frames.clear();
435.                     // Free remaining un-wrapped frames from the contiguous allocation.
436.                     for j in i..count {
437.                         let leak_raw: usize = base_raw + j * mem::PAGE_SIZE;
438.                         if let Ok(fa) = FrameAddress::from_raw_value(leak_raw) {
439.                             if let Err(e) = frame::free(fa) {
440.                                 warn!("failed to free leaked frame {fa:?}: {e:?}");
441.                             }
442.                         }
443.                     }
444.                     return Err(e);
445.                 },
446.             }
447.         }

5. //
6. // `PhysMemoryManager` is a *stateless* facade over the global frame allocator
7. // (`Upool` carries no fields; kernel frames are drawn directly from `frame::*`).

9. // state is the global frame-reservation state, modelled by the do-not-modify
10. // `phys_view()` / `FrameAllocView` in `mod.spec.rs`. All manager contracts are
11. // stated over `phys_view()` and the returned frame values -- exactly the monotone
12. // style used by the `frame::*` free-function shims (`book`, `alloc_range`, ...).
13. //
14. // See `verus-ai-logs/nanvix-phys-phys-manager/view_design.md` for why a bespoke
15. // `self@` View is *not* realizable here (a constant view cannot witness global
16. // mutation, and there is no `old(phys_view())`).

21. use crate::mm::phys::{
22.     phys_view,
23.     FrameAllocView,
24. };
25. use vstd::seq::Seq;
26. 
27. /// The kernel watermark threshold, lifted to `int`.
28. ///
29. /// Abstract (uninterpreted) form of the build-time constant
30. /// `config::kernel::KERNEL_WATERMARK`: the number of physical frames the
31. /// allocator must keep in reserve for kernel use, below which user allocations
32. /// are refused. It is left opaque because the concrete value is a build-time
33. /// constant of an external crate; callers only rely on its consistency, not its
34. /// magnitude.
35. pub uninterp spec fn spec_kernel_watermark() -> int;
36. 
37. /// A user allocation of `count` frames is admissible only if, after servicing it,
38. /// at least `KERNEL_WATERMARK` frames would still be free.
39. ///
40. /// Stated on the abstract free-set cardinality -- never on an allocator counter --
41. /// so it survives any frame-allocator reimplementation. `free_frames.len()` is
42. /// meaningful because the allocator keeps `free_frames` finite (see the shim
43. /// contracts, which (re)establish `phys_view().frames.free_frames.finite()`).
44. pub open spec fn spec_watermark_ok(v: FrameAllocView, count: int) -> bool {
45.     v.free_frames.len() >= spec_kernel_watermark() + count
46. }
47. 
48. /// `addrs` is an ascending, page-stride-contiguous run of frame addresses based
49. /// at `base`: `addrs[i] == base + i * PAGE_SIZE`.
50. ///
51. /// Used to state the contiguity guarantee of `alloc_many_kernel_frames` over the
52. /// sequence of returned kernel-frame addresses (kernel stacks require a linear,
53. /// identity-mapped physical region).
54. pub open spec fn is_contiguous_run(addrs: Seq<int>, base: int) -> bool {
55.     forall|i: int|
56.         0 <= i < addrs.len() ==> #[trigger] addrs[i] == base + i * spec_page_size()
57. }
58.

60. /// `base`: the address of the `i`-th frame is `base + i * PAGE_SIZE`.
61. ///
62. /// Phrased directly over the `KernelFrame` sequence (using each frame's abstract
63. /// address `@`) so that the `alloc_many_kernel_frames` contiguity guarantee can be
64. /// triggered without an inline closure (closures are forbidden inside triggers).
65. pub open spec fn kernel_frames_contiguous(frames: Seq<KernelFrame>, base: int) -> bool {
66.     forall|i: int|
67.         0 <= i < frames.len() ==> #[trigger] frames[i]@ == base + i * spec_page_size()
68. }

# Build everything with the local toolchain.
./z build -- all

# Kernel only.
./z build -- kernel

./z build -- all-nanvixd
